title: Compose production Streamable HTTP MCP host
description: Objective: land the real daemon consumer for the already root-published official Streamable HTTP MCP adapter, using the same bounded authenticated dispatch authority as stdio. Deliverable: daemon host/composition code and focused tests that start the official adapter, route requests through production authentication/dispatch, and shut down without alternate command semantics. NOT in scope: custom WebSocket, UI APIs, portability evidence, or new daemon commands. Measured at HEAD 30458af: createHttpMcpAdapter is public from @moe/mcp (task-8ce8b35cb27d44009bb7c44a9ba85fc6), apps/daemon declares @moe/mcp and pnpm-lock links it, but only createStdioMcpServer/connectStdioTransport are called in apps/daemon/src/mcp-main.ts; createHttpMcpAdapter has zero production callers. Coordinate with existing task-49ed1e6d73544fc6ae09b3951a573848 if it becomes buildable; do not duplicate a landed host. Consumers: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 and task-49ed1e6d73544fc6ae09b3951a573848. Owned paths: a focused apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/** module/test set and minimal daemon executable/manifest wiring.
definitionOfDone: A production daemon entry point constructs createHttpMcpAdapter from the bare @moe/mcp root and connects it to the same authenticated command/query dispatcher used by stdio; no test dispatcher or deep import grants authority.
Official Streamable HTTP session, resume, cancellation, bounds, and disconnect outcomes preserve exact transport and daemon reason code/layer and commit nothing on refusal.
Startup and graceful shutdown own the listener/session lifecycle exactly once; restart reuses durable daemon state without custom WebSocket or alternate lifecycle semantics.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the authority mapping, in a new apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-session-port.test.ts. This is the only genuinely new authority decision in the task and it must be pinned case by case against the REAL production authenticator (createSessionAuthenticator over a real SqliteEventStore), never a fake: the daemon's AuthenticationResult has three arms and @moe/mcp's HttpAuthVerdict has two, so the mapping is exact and closed. Cases, each asserting the EXACT code: an authenticated operator credential yields ok:true with principalRef copied verbatim from principal.principalId and sessionRef equal to it; an authenticated SESSION credential yields ok:true whose principalRef is the session id, because session-authenticator.ts:138 deliberately returns `match.sessionId` as the working principal; an unknown or malformed credential yields AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; a credential bound to a prior recovery incarnation yields SESSION_REPLAYED VERBATIM, since that is the daemon's own PortRefusal code and the seam holds no translation table; an EXPIRED session yields AUTHENTICATION_FAILED and explicitly NOT SESSION_EXPIRED — assert both halves, because the daemon returns UNAUTHENTICATED for expiry on purpose and mapping it to SESSION_EXPIRED would hand a caller an oracle the authenticator refuses to give; and a REFUSED verdict carrying any code outside HTTP_AUTH_REFUSAL_CODES fails closed to AUTHENTICATION_FAILED rather than being forwarded. Assert the four-member HTTP_AUTH_REFUSAL_CODES vocabulary is consumed as-is and that no new refusal vocabulary is declared anywhere under mcp-http/. Reuse apps/daemon/src/identity/session-test-fixtures.ts and the state shapes recovery-authentication.test.ts already builds rather than hand-rolling ledger rows. Open every store handle inside the `it` body with try/finally — a handle held across an afterEach rmSync fails with EPERM on Windows and kills the vitest worker with zero output. Run and record the RED.

implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-session-port.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./mcp-http-session-port.ts";`, LF, matching every sibling daemon module). Export one factory taking the daemon's existing `Authenticator` and returning an `HttpSessionPort` typed from the bare `@moe/mcp` root. validateBearer re-runs `authenticator.authenticate(credential)` on EVERY call with no memoisation — the port contract says revalidating each time is exactly what makes a rotated or revoked credential die on the next request — and maps the three daemon arms onto the two MCP arms with the closed table from step 2. principalRef and sessionRef are COPIED from the principal, never minted, never a credential, and never derived from request bytes. bindSession and closeSession maintain only an in-process map of mcpSessionId to the accepted verdict, so close is idempotent and exactly-once; they must NOT write a durable session record, because minting sessions is `session.open`'s job and doing it here would be the second authentication policy rail 2 forbids. Document why SESSION_EXPIRED and CAPABILITY_DENIED are members this daemon never selects. Keep the file well under the 250-line target.

SHAPE. One factory `createMcpHttpSessionPort(authenticator: Authenticator): McpHttpSessionPort`. validateBearer calls authenticator.authenticate on EVERY invocation with no memoisation and no cache — the closed-session test drives the SAME port instance before and after session.close and requires the second call to refuse, so the absence of memoisation is pinned by behaviour, not by comment. principalRef and sessionRef are COPIED from principal.principalId; nothing is minted, hashed, compared or derived from request bytes in this file. bindSession/closeSession maintain only an in-process Map of transport id -> accepted verdict; Map.set makes re-bind idempotent and Map.delete makes double-close a no-op, and the test pins committed-decision-count equality across bind/close so transport binding provably writes nothing durable.

MAPPING, closed: AUTHENTICATED -> ok:true; REFUSED -> code forwarded verbatim only if it is one of the four MCP codes, else AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; UNAUTHENTICATED -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. The fail-closed branch runs through a runtime Set, so a daemon code added later that MCP does not define cannot reach a client as an invented member.

TYPES DERIVED, NOT DEEP-IMPORTED (same forced deviation disclosed in step 2): Verdict = Awaited<ReturnType<HttpSessionPort["validateBearer"]>>, Accepted = Parameters<HttpSessionPort["bindSession"]>[1], RefusalCode = Extract<Verdict,{ok:false}>["code"]. Only `HttpSessionPort` is imported, from the bare `@moe/mcp` root. No import in this module reaches past a package root.

SESSION_EXPIRED and CAPABILITY_DENIED are documented in the source as deliberately never selected: expiry is folded into AUTHENTICATION_FAILED so a caller cannot use refusal codes as an oracle separating "expired" from "unknown", and capability is authorization decided behind the dispatch port against a command this credential-only screen never sees.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the host, in a new apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts, driving the REAL pipeline end to end: a real temp-file SqliteEventStore, real readStoreDependencyEnv/createStoreDependencies, the real createMcpDispatchPort, the real session authenticator, and the real createHttpMcpAdapter — no test dispatcher and no deep import may grant authority, or the test proves only shapes. Cases: (1) LIFECYCLE — start binds on port 0, reports the assigned port, and a SECOND start on the same host refuses rather than binding twice; stop closes the listener AND the adapter exactly once, a second stop is a no-op, and — critically — a start/stop/start/stop cycle completes, because an HTTP server that omits closeAllConnections passes a single teardown and hangs on the second, which is precisely the restart DoD 3 requires. (2) DISPATCH — an initialize request with a valid credential mints a session, and a tools/call over that session returns the daemon's own answer produced by handleCommandRequest, proving the request reached the production pipeline rather than a stub. (3) REFUSAL PRESERVES CODE AND LAYER — an unknown credential is refused with the exact transport status and the exact stable code the registry owns, no daemon internals in the message. (4) COMMITS NOTHING ON REFUSAL — read the store's committed decision count before and after each refused request and assert it is IDENTICAL; this is the assertion that makes 'refusal commits nothing' mechanically checkable rather than asserted in prose. (5) BRIDGE FIDELITY — a request driven through the real node listener socket produces the same status, headers and body as the same Request handed straight to adapter.handleRequest, so the node-to-Web bridge cannot silently drop a header the MCP session protocol needs (the session id header above all). Assert a hand-written case count. Store handles open and close inside each `it`; bound every await so a hung transport fails by name instead of stalling the suite. Run and record the RED.

(2) RESTART — start/stop/start/stop completes, then a third stop is a no-op; this is the case a single teardown cannot see, since a node:http server missing closeAllConnections closes cleanly once and hangs on a kept-alive socket the second time. implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts plus its `.js` bridge. It does exactly three things. (a) Builds the adapter: `createHttpMcpAdapter({ dispatchPort, sessionPort })` where dispatchPort is the value returned by the existing createMcpDispatchPort — a StdioDispatchPort is assignable to HttpDispatchPort by construction (http-tool-bridge.ts:26 documents the port width as a deliberate superset), so no second dispatcher, no second envelope vocabulary, and no adapter-side authority is created. (b) Owns a node:http listener that bridges IncomingMessage to a Web Request and writes the Web Response back, modelled on apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts including its `server.closeAllConnections?.()` on shutdown (line 246) — that call is the difference between a teardown that passes once and one that survives a restart. Preserve every header in both directions verbatim; the MCP session id header is protocol state, not decoration. (c) Exposes start/stop with single-ownership semantics: start binds once and returns the bound address, a second start refuses, stop closes listener then adapter and is idempotent. No routing table beyond the single MCP endpoint, no custom WebSocket, no alternate lifecycle. If the file approaches 250 physical lines, split the node-to-Web bridging into its own module plus bridge rather than trimming the lifecycle comments.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 5 — host implemented; steps 2 and 4 are GREEN.

FILES (`grep -c ''`, all under the 250 target): mcp-http-host.ts 176, mcp-http-node-bridge.ts 92, mcp-http-session-port.ts 114. Tests 345 + 296. Both new production modules have LF `.js` bridges.

I SPLIT THE BRIDGE OUT, as the step authorised. mcp-http-node-bridge.ts owns IncomingMessage<->Web framing only; the host owns lifecycle. Headers travel verbatim both ways and multi-value headers are APPENDED rather than joined, since joining is lossy for repeated protocol headers. GET/HEAD/DELETE deliberately carry no body — the SDK distinguishes "no body" from "empty body" when routing a resumption. Responses are STREAMED back, not buffered, because SSE is the adapter's default mode and a buffered read would never resolve for a live event stream.

NO SECOND AUTHORITY. dispatchPort is the value createMcpDispatchPort already returns — the same one mcp-main.ts uses — so commands still run through handleCommandRequest verbatim. No second dispatcher, no second envelope vocabulary, no adapter-side authority. Loopback-only bind, refusing to START with MCP_HTTP_HOST_NON_LOOPBACK_BIND rather than warning. Host lifecycle refusals are their own closed 3-code vocabulary and never overlap the MCP auth vocabulary.

A DESIGN CONFLICT IN THE PLAN THAT I HAD TO RESOLVE, disclosed. Step 5 says stop() closes listener THEN adapter; DoD 3 requires restart. Those are incompatible if the adapter is host-scoped — stop would close the only adapter and the next start would come back up unable to serve. I made the adapter LIFECYCLE-scoped: built on demand, closed and cleared by stop, rebuilt by the next start. stop clears both fields BEFORE any await, so a repeated or concurrent stop cannot double-close, and closes listener before adapter so a socket cannot race a live transport against its own teardown. closeAllConnections?.() is present and is the reason the start/stop/start/stop case passes.

THREE FAILURES I DIAGNOSED AS TEST DEFECTS, NOT PRODUCTION DEFECTS — and the evidence for that call, since "the test was wrong" is the easy wrong answer:
1+2. Direct in-process requests returned 403 CAPABILITY_DENIED and socket requests 406. Cause: `new Request(url, ...)` does NOT derive a `host` header from the URL, and the adapter screens Host/Origin for loopback ITSELF (http-server.ts:110) rather than delegating; separately the Streamable HTTP transport requires `accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. The producer's own helper (http-server-test-helpers.ts:37) sets both headers explicitly for exactly this reason. A real client always sends both and the socket path already carried host, so production was never wrong — my in-process requests were under-specified. Fixed in the test via one mcpRequest() builder.
3. tools/call returned INPUT_INVALID. Cause: the runtime QUERY envelope is EXACT-KEYED (`hasExactKeys` over correlationId/queryKind/schemaVersion/sessionCredential/payload, runtime-envelope.ts:190) and my args omitted correlationId, so it was refused at decode before the dispatch port was consulted. Note this refusal still proved the pipeline was reached — it carried the daemon's registryVersion and truthClass DAEMON_VERIFIED.

THE DISPATCH ASSERTION CHANGED, and it is now stronger. I originally expected a successful page containing "items". A fresh store has no cursor generation, so the REAL readSubscriptionPage refuses with `{"code":"SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION_MISSING","layer":"STATE","outcome":"REFUSED"}`. Rather than build subscription state to manufacture a success, I pin that exact code AND layer: the pair is produced by the production read model over the production store and by nothing else, so a canned success or any stub fails it — which is precisely what drill D6 will demonstrate. This also satisfies epic rail 6 (assert the reason code and the refusing layer, never merely "not ok") better than a success-shape check would have.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills. For each: sha256 first, edit with the Edit tool, confirm the anchor matched once, run only the named test, reverse the edit, confirm the sha256 is restored (never git checkout — it reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree). D1: map an expired session to SESSION_EXPIRED instead of AUTHENTICATION_FAILED — the no-oracle case reddens on the exact code, proving the mapping is pinned and not incidental. D2: forward an out-of-vocabulary daemon refusal code verbatim — the fail-closed case reddens. D3: memoise validateBearer after the first success — the revocation case reddens, proving re-validation per request is real. D4: delete `closeAllConnections` from stop — the start/stop/start/stop restart case reddens or hangs; if it hangs, that IS the finding, and the bound on the wait is what turns it into a named failure instead of a stalled suite. D5: drop the session id header in the node-to-Web bridge — the bridge-fidelity comparison reddens on the named header rather than on a vague status mismatch. D6: return a canned success from the dispatch path instead of calling the production port — the dispatch case must redden, proving the test is wired to the real pipeline and not to a shape. Read each failure message and confirm it names the assertion the drill targets; a red for the wrong reason means the drill is broken, not that the guard is proven.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 7 — six mutation drills. ALL SIX NOW KILL, but D4 did not at first and that is the most important thing in this note. Final suite: EXIT 0, 2 files, 21 tests.

Every drill: sha256 first, mutated with the Edit tool (never a shell one-liner), only the named test run, reversed with Edit, hash re-checked. `git checkout` was never used — it reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree.

D1 expired -> SESSION_EXPIRED instead of AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: RED. Named case "maps an EXPIRED session ... explicitly NOT SESSION_EXPIRED" failed with `expected { code: 'SESSION_EXPIRED' } to deeply equal { code: 'AUTHENTICATION_FAILED' }`. 5 cases red total — correct, since the mutation moves every UNAUTHENTICATED arm.
D2 forward an out-of-vocabulary code verbatim: RED, exactly ONE case, `expected { code: 'PROJECT_QUARANTINED' } to deeply equal { code: 'AUTHENTICATION_FAILED' }`.
D3 memoise validateBearer after first success: RED, exactly ONE case, the revocation case — `expected { ok: true } to deeply equal { code: 'AUTHENTICATION_FAILED' }`. Re-validation per request is real.
D5 drop the session id header in the bridge: RED, exactly the bridge-fidelity case, `expected null not to be null` on the socket-side session header.
D6 canned success instead of the production dispatch port: RED, exactly the dispatch case, received `{"items":[],"ok":true}` where the daemon's `SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION_MISSING` was required.

D4 SURVIVED TWICE AND EXPOSED TWO REAL DEFECTS. This is the finding of the step; I did not rewrite a good test to make a drill pass.
  Attempt 1 — deleting closeAllConnections left the suite GREEN. Cause: my restart case did start/stop/start/stop without ever making a request, so no socket existed at teardown and the condition was never exercised. A test that cannot fail is not evidence.
  Attempt 2 — added a real keep-alive fetch to each cycle. STILL GREEN. Rather than guess again I measured the premise directly with a standalone node probe: response `connection: keep-alive`, `getConnections` = 1, and `server.close()` still fired its callback. So the widely-repeated claim in the plan and in http-listener.ts's comment — "a server without closeAllConnections passes a single teardown and hangs on the second" — is FALSE on this Node version for IDLE sockets. Since Node 19, close() reaps them itself. D4 was an equivalent mutant against every test I had.
  Attempt 3 — the distinction that actually matters is ACTIVE vs idle: close() waits on active connections, and this adapter's default transport mode is SSE, a stream that stays open by design. I added a case that opens the event stream with a GET, deliberately does NOT drain it, and then stops. D4 now KILLS with `TIMED OUT waiting for: stop with SSE stream open` — the bounded await turning a hang into a named failure, which is exactly what the step asked for.
  THAT NEW CASE IMMEDIATELY FOUND A PRODUCTION BUG IN MY OWN BRIDGE. The SSE GET never resolved at the client even with correct production code: node holds response headers until the first body write, and an event stream that has not yet emitted writes nothing, so the client blocked forever waiting for headers. Fixed with `target.flushHeaders()` before streaming. This is a real defect that only the SSE case could surface, and it would have shipped.

D6 ALSO INDICTED AN EARLIER ASSERTION OF MINE. My original dispatch assertion was `expect(text).toContain("items")`. The canned stub returns `{"items":[],"ok":true}` — it CONTAINS "items", so the original assertion would have passed the drill and D6 would have read as green. It only became lethal because step 5 changed the assertion to the daemon's stable SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION_MISSING / layer STATE pair. A drill is only as sharp as the assertion under it.

RESTORE EVIDENCE, stated precisely because two hashes deliberately differ from pre-drill:
  mcp-http-session-port.ts ec4a4295...f8c7 — IDENTICAL to pre-drill (D1/D2/D3 fully reversed).
  mcp-dispatch-port.ts 7e1178b4...8124 — IDENTICAL; never mutated, listed only to prove the foreign file was untouched.
  mcp-http-node-bridge.ts d67ca960 -> 734887d0 — CHANGED ON PURPOSE: the flushHeaders fix above.
  mcp-http-host.ts 03b2f18d -> 90b3bc40 — CHANGED ON PURPOSE: the closeAllConnections comment now records the measured Node-19 nuance instead of repeating the folklore.
  Residue check, mutation by mutation: D1 SESSION_EXPIRED return 0 hits; D2 isForwardable guard 1 hit; D4 closeAllConnections 1 hit; D5 "mcp-session-id" in the bridge 0 hits; D6 real createMcpDispatchPort 1 hit and canned-stub arrow 0 hits. THE ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND A REAL CONCURRENCY BUG THAT NO TEST WOULD HAVE CAUGHT, and I fixed it before finishing. `start()` checked `server !== null` but assigned `server` only AFTER awaiting `listen` — textbook check-then-act. Every existing case awaited sequentially, so the window was invisible. I wrote a case firing three `start()` calls without awaiting between them and drilled it (D7) by reverting to the unserialised form: ALL THREE SUCCEEDED — three listeners bound, two orphaned with no reference left to close them, a permanent socket and fd leak on any host that starts twice concurrently. Fixed by serialising every lifecycle transition through a promise chain, so a later caller observes the earlier one's committed result. With the fix: 1 accepted, 2 refused MCP_HTTP_HOST_ALREADY_STARTED, and the accepted origin is provably the reachable one. Host restored byte-exact (c88adac1...0fda) after the drill.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED: mounting the MCP adapter inside the existing apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts — that listener is the daemon's own command/query API with its own guards and refusal vocabulary, and adding a second protocol to it would entangle two transports in one lifecycle; the task's owned paths call for a focused mcp-http/** module set and a separate entry, mirroring how mcp-main.ts sits beside daemon-main.ts. REJECTED: writing a new dispatch port for HTTP — http-tool-bridge.ts:26 documents HttpDispatchPort as a deliberate SUPERSET of the stdio port shape, so the value createMcpDispatchPort already returns is assignable unchanged; building another would be the second dispatcher rail 2 forbids. REJECTED: minting a durable session record in bindSession — session.open is the daemon command that owns session creation, and doing it at the transport would be a second authentication policy. REJECTED: mapping an expired session to SESSION_EXPIRED — the daemon's authenticator deliberately answers UNAUTHENTICATED for unknown, malformed, closed AND expired credentials so a caller cannot use refusal codes as an oracle; the HTTP vocabulary happens to contain SESSION_EXPIRED, but selecting it would leak exactly the distinction the authenticator refuses to give. Both halves of that decision are asserted in step 2 and drilled in step 7. REJECTED: driving the tests through a fake dispatcher — global rail clause 2 is explicit that a proof which only proves the shapes is worse than none; the host test therefore runs a real store, the real store dependencies, the real dispatch port and the real authenticator, and D6 drills that wiring.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED at HEAD 7dbf9ba, 2026-08-14 (description's HEAD 30458af is stale).

GAP OPEN, CONFIRMED. `grep -rn createHttpMcpAdapter --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` hits ONLY packages/mcp: http-server.ts:244 (the definition), index.ts:28 (the root export), and four of its own test/helper files. ZERO hits under apps/daemon/src. The public adapter genuinely has no production consumer.

EDGE PRESENT. apps/daemon/package.json declares `"@moe/mcp": "workspace:*"` and apps/daemon/src/mcp-main.ts already imports connectStdioTransport/createStdioMcpServer/readBootstrapCredential from the bare root, so the import path is proven live; step 1 still re-runs the compiled bare-specifier probe because the rail demands the probe, not the precedent.

THE TWO PORTS THE ADAPTER NEEDS. packages/mcp/src/http/http-server.ts:49-56 — HttpAdapterOptions is {dispatchPort, sessionPort, enableJsonResponse?, serverName?, sessionIdFactory?}; :58-61 — HttpMcpAdapter is {close(), handleRequest(Request): Promise<Response>}, i.e. NOT a listener, so the daemon must own the node:http server and bridge IncomingMessage/ServerResponse to Web Request/Response. No such bridge exists in production code anywhere in the repo today (`grep 'new Request('` finds only packages/mcp/src/http/http-server-test-helpers.ts:48), so the host writes one.

DISPATCH PORT IS ALREADY SOLVED. http-tool-bridge.ts:26-33 states HttpDispatchPort accepts an optional AbortSignal and tolerates async results, both supersets of the stdio shape, so a StdioDispatchPort is assignable. apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.ts:50 createMcpDispatchPort returns exactly that and routes commands through handleCommandRequest verbatim.

SESSION PORT IS THE ONE NEW DECISION. packages/mcp/src/http/http-session.ts:30-62 — HttpSessionPort is {validateBearer, bindSession, closeSession}; the accepted arm carries opaque principalRef and sessionRef, and refusals are closed to exactly AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, CAPABILITY_DENIED, SESSION_EXPIRED, SESSION_REPLAYED. The daemon side is apps/daemon/src/http/http-contract.ts:99-117 — Authenticator.authenticate(credential) returns AUTHENTICATED with AuthenticatedPrincipal {capabilities, principalId, projectId}, REFUSED with PortRefusal {code, detail, httpStatus, layer}, or UNAUTHENTICATED. Mapping facts measured in apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authenticator.ts: line 138 returns `match.sessionId` as the principalId for a session credential (the working principal IS the session), lines 100-133 return UNAUTHENTICATED for null/empty/unknown/ambiguous/closed/unreadable AND for expired, and the ONLY REFUSED constant in the file is RECOVERY_REPLAYED at :47-55 carrying code SESSION_REPLAYED, layer IDENTITY. So SESSION_REPLAYED forwards verbatim, everything else lands on AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, and a closed check keeps any future daemon code fail-closed.

LIFECYCLE PRECEDENT. apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts uses node:http createServer at :208, listens at :220, and calls `server.closeAllConnections?.()` at :246 — copy that, because a server without it passes a single teardown and hangs on the second, which is exactly the restart DoD 3 asks for.

ENTRY PRECEDENT. apps/daemon/src/mcp-main.ts (63 lines) is the shape to mirror: shebang, env read, createStoreDependencies, a SECOND read handle on the same store file, DatabaseSync with busy_timeout, `import.meta.main` guard, named export for in-process tests. It has no `.js` bridge because nothing imports it; every imported daemon module (daemon-entry.js, mcp-dispatch-port.js) does have one. apps/daemon/package.json currently exposes only `moe-daemon` in bin.
planningNotes.risks:
1. A SHAPE-ONLY PROOF WOULD FAIL THIS TASK'S WHOLE PURPOSE. The point is a real consumer edge; a host test driven by a fake dispatcher proves the adapter's own suite over again. Real store, real dependencies, real port, real authenticator — and D6 exists to prove that wiring is load-bearing.
2. TEARDOWN THAT PASSES ONCE. A node:http server without closeAllConnections closes cleanly the first time and hangs the second; a single start/stop test would never see it. The restart case is mandatory and every await in it must be bounded so a hang fails by name rather than stalling the suite.
3. HELD SQLITE HANDLE KILLS THE VITEST WORKER. On Windows an open handle makes the temp-dir cleanup throw EPERM and the run dies with zero test output, reading as a native crash. Open and close inside each `it`, never in a describe body.
4. THE REFUSAL VOCABULARY IS CLOSED BY THE PRODUCER. @moe/mcp is DONE and not ours to widen, so the daemon must map into its four codes. Forward SESSION_REPLAYED verbatim, fail closed on anything unmapped, and never invent a fifth code or a translation table in the other direction.
5. DO NOT LEAK AN ORACLE. Expiry, unknown credentials and closed sessions must remain indistinguishable at the wire, matching the authenticator's deliberate silence.
6. HEADER FIDELITY. The MCP session id header is protocol state; a bridge that drops or renames a header breaks resume in a way a status-code assertion will not catch, which is why step 4 compares a socket-driven response against a direct handleRequest response.
7. DUPLICATE-HOST HAZARD. task-49ed1e6d may land the same consumer; step 1's grep is the check, and rail 3 says report the gap closed rather than duplicate.
8. SHARED WORKTREE. Other agents hold uncommitted work under .moe/**, packages/store/**, packages/contracts/** and packages/runner/**. Never git add -A, never stash, never reset; git add the new files explicitly before committing by pathspec.
